By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United 
States and as Commander in Chief of the armed forces of the United 
States, I  hereby authorize the Secretary of Defense, with respect to 
members of the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Marine Corps, and the 
Secretary of the Treasury, with respect to members of the Coast Guard 
when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, to prescribe regula­
tions under which the United Nations Medal and Service Ribbon may 
be accepted by members of the armed forces who have been determined 
eligible for consideration in accordance with the Regulations for the 
United Nations Medal, promulgated by the United Nations Organiza­
tion on July 30, 1959. A determination that service with the United 
Nations in a particular geographic area or for a particular purpose 
constitutes a justifiable basis for authorizing acceptance of the United 
Nations Medal and Service Ribbon by eligible members of the armed 
forces of the United States shall be made with the concurrence of 
the Secretary of State.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The paragraph authorizes the Secretary of Defense, for the Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps, and (as originally written) the Secretary of the Treasury, for the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, to prescribe regulations under which the United Nations Medal and Service Ribbon may be accepted by eligible members of the armed forces, and requires the Secretary of State's concurrence in determinations about service areas and purposes. Executive Order 13286 section 68, effective March 1, 2003 (section 92), struck the words the Secretary of the Treasury and inserted the Secretary of Homeland Security (before: the Secretary of the Treasury; after: the Secretary of Homeland Security). The clause continues as amended; the held text of the paragraph has no end date or condition, and no later order revoking or superseding it was found. It is operative on 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11139 of January 7, 1964 (29 FR 227; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11139.txt, read in full) is a single paragraph. It authorizes the Secretary of Defense (for members of the Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps) and the Secretary of the Treasury (for members of the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy) to prescribe regulations under which the United Nations Medal and Service Ribbon may be accepted by eligible members of the armed forces, and requires that a determination that service in a particular area or for a particular purpose is a justifiable basis for acceptance be made with the concurrence of the Secretary of State. The text states no date, duration, condition or expiry. The only later instrument found is Executive Order 13286 section 68 (68 FR 10619, 10629; effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92), which struck the Secretary of the Treasury and inserted the Secretary of Homeland Security; it is recorded as a later event on the clause. A search of the held Federal Register texts of orders numbered above 11139 for citations of this order found only Executive Order 13286. The Office of the Federal Register disposition note for the order reads that it was amended by Executive Order 13286, February 28, 2003, and names no revocation or supersession. The bounded searches current-law:usc (one hit, the printed Executive Order 13286 note listing section 68 as an amendment of this order), current-law:ecfr (no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (one hit, the Executive Order 13286 amendment) show no revocation. The clause is therefore operative on 2026-10-14. No current Code or CFR text printing this order is held, so the current predicate rests on the held original, the held amendment and the three bounded searches (the original_plus_bounded_search route). THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 11965 • January 19, 1977
Establishing the Humanitarian Service Medal
By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United States of 
America, and as Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces, it is hereby ordered 
as follows:
Section  1. There'' is hereby established a Humanitarian Service Medal with 
accompanying ribbons and appurtenances for award by the Secretary of Defense 
or the Secretary of Transportation with regard to the Coast Guard when not operating 
as a Service in the Navy. Individuals eligible for the medal are members of the Armed *  
Forces of the United States (including Reserve Components) who, subsequent to 
April 1, 1975, distinguished themselves by meritorious participation in a military act 
or operation of a humanitarian nature. The Secretary of Defense and the Secretary 
of Transportation for the Coast Guard will determine types of acts or operations that 
warrant award of the medal.
Sec. 2. The Humanitarian Service Medal and ribbons and appurtenances thereto 
shall be of appropriate design approved by the Secretary of Defense and shall be 
awarded by the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Transportation for the 
Coast Guard under uniform regulations, as prescribed by the Secretary of Defense. 
The regulations shall place the Humanitarian Service Medal in an order of precedence 
immediately after the Vietnam Service Medal.
Sec. 3. No more than one Humanitarian Service Medal shall be awarded to 
any one person, but for each subsequent participation in a humanitarian act or 
operation justifying such an award, a suitable device may be awarded to be worn with 
that medal as prescribed by appropriate regulations of the Military Departments.
Sec. 4. The Humanitarian Service Medal or device may be awarded post­
humously, and when so awarded, may be presented to such representative of the 
deceased as may be deemed appropriate by the Secretary of Defense or the Secretary 
of Transportation.
• * /

research_rationale:
Executive Order 11965 of January 19, 1977 (42 FR 4329; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11965.txt, read in full) has four sections: section 1 establishes the Humanitarian Service Medal with ribbons and appurtenances, for award by the Secretary of Defense or, for the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, the Secretary of Transportation, and sets eligibility (members of the Armed Forces who after April 1, 1975 distinguished themselves by meritorious participation in a military act or operation of a humanitarian nature); section 2 provides for the design, uniform regulations and order of precedence; section 3 limits the medal to one per person with devices for later participation; section 4 allows posthumous award. The text states no date, duration, condition or expiry. The only later instrument found is Executive Order 13286 section 55 (68 FR 10619, 10629; effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92), which struck the Secretary of Transportation wherever it appears in sections 1, 2 and 4 and inserted the Secretary of Homeland Security; it is recorded as a later event on sections 1, 2 and 4 and does not touch section 3. A search of the held Federal Register texts of orders numbered above 11965 for citations of this order found only Executive Order 13286. The Office of the Federal Register note records only the Executive Order 13286 amendment. The U.S. Code prints the order as amended under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 note (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09). The three bounded searches show no revocation. All four sections are operative on 2026-10-14.
